trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Sercotel Porta Barcelona
hotel.location: Generalitat de Catalunya, 6, Sant Just Desvern, ES (41.3772,2.0791)

experiences.description: Explore Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica with a skip-the-line guided tour. Marvel at the intricate facades, stunning stained glass windows, and learn about the century-long construction history. Climb the towers for panoramic city views.

experiences.name: La Boqueria Market Food Experience
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in Barcelona's legendary public market on La Rambla. Sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico, local cheeses, seafood, and fresh-squeezed juices from the vibrant stalls. A true feast for the senses and a cultural institution since 1217.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the L9 Sud metro line to Torrassa, then transfer to L1 toward Sant Just Desvern area, or take a budget bus (Aerobús ~€6.75) to Plaça Catalunya. Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona. Once settled, take a short stroll around the nearby Sant Just Desvern neighborhood to get oriented and grab a casual bite.

meals.dinner: Bar or local tavern near the hotel in Sant Just Desvern — look for a menú del día or bocadillo (sandwich) for €5–8. Try Bar Restaurant Can Rafel or any neighborhood bar serving tapas.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you're arriving late. Grab a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) at the airport to save on transport all week. Hydrate and rest early; big days ahead. August heat averages 28.9°C so pack light, breathable clothing.

day_by_day.morning: Head into central Barcelona via metro (L1 or bus). Visit the Gothic Quarter on a self-guided or free walking tour starting around 9:30 AM before the heat peaks. Explore the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 PM), Plaça Reial, Roman ruins of Barcino, and the narrow medieval lanes. Many free walking tours depart from Plaça de la Catalunya around 10:00 AM (tip-based, budget ~€5–10 tip).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to La Boqueria Market on La Rambla for the La Boqueria Market Food Experience. Arrive around 13:00 to sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico, olives, and fresh fruit. Budget €10–15 for grazing. Afterward, explore El Raval neighborhood and visit the MACBA (Museum of Contemporary Art) exterior plaza — a popular skate spot and great for architecture photography. If budget allows, MACBA entry is €12 but the exterior is free.
day_by_day.evening: As the sun sets, head to the El Born neighborhood for pre-dinner drinks at a budget bar. Explore the Palau de la Música Catalana exterior (a UNESCO-listed Modernista gem — free to admire outside). Then enjoy Barcelona's early nightlife scene — El Born and the Gothic Quarter bars get lively from 21:00 onward. Try a craft beer or vermouth at a local bar.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant or pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato) at a local café near the hotel or in the Gothic Quarter — budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Graze at La Boqueria Market — fresh fruit, a bocadillo, or a small tapa plate. Budget €10–15.
meals.dinner: El Born neighborhood — look for a menú del día (even at dinner some places offer it) or a budget pintxos bar. Try Bar del Pla or similar spots for €12–18 per person including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Gothic Quarter has uneven cobblestones. Carry a refillable water bottle; public drinking fountains (fonts) are available throughout the city. Avoid peak midday heat (14:00–16:00) by resting in a shaded plaza or café.

day_by_day.morning: Book the Sagrada Família Guided Tour in advance online (skip-the-line tickets ~€26–33 with tower access). Arrive at opening time (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds and the worst of the heat. The guided tour lasts approximately 1.5–2 hours. Marvel at Gaudí's extraordinary unfinished basilica — the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like interior columns, and the stained glass light show.
day_by_day.afternoon: After Sagrada Família, walk or take a short metro ride to the Eixample district to explore Gaudí's architectural legacy on a self-guided Modernisme walk. See Casa Batlló and Casa Milà (La Pedrera) exteriors for free along Passeig de Gràcia — the 'Block of Discord' also features Casa Amatller and Casa Lleó Morera. If budget allows, Casa Batlló night experience is spectacular but pricey (~€35); stick to exterior admiration to save money. Rest during peak heat (14:00–16:00) at a shaded café.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Gràcia neighborhood for dinner — a bohemian, local area with budget-friendly restaurants and lively plazas. After dinner, explore the nightlife in Gràcia or head back toward El Born. For late-night architecture lovers, the illuminated Sagrada Família at night is stunning and completely free to view from outside.

meals.breakfast: Café near Sagrada Família — coffee and a pastry for €3–5. Try a local bakery (forn de pa) rather than tourist cafés.
meals.lunch: Menú del día in the Eixample — a 3-course lunch with bread and a drink for €12–15. This is the best budget meal deal in Spain.
meals.dinner: Gràcia neighborhood — La Pepita or similar budget-friendly spots. Tapas and a drink for €12–16 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets at least 2–3 weeks in advance for August — it sells out fast. The guided tour adds significant value for architecture enthusiasts. Wear sunscreen; the walk along Passeig de Gràcia is fully exposed to the sun.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or bus to Parc Güell (another Gaudí masterpiece). The Monumental Zone requires a timed ticket (~€10, book online in advance). Arrive at 9:00 AM opening for cooler temperatures and fewer crowds. Explore the mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and panoramic views over Barcelona. The surrounding park areas outside the paid zone are free and equally beautiful for a morning stroll.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Parc Güell and head to the Barceloneta beach neighborhood. Spend the hottest part of the day (14:00–17:00) cooling off at Barceloneta Beach — completely free. Walk along the Passeig Marítim boardwalk, explore the Port Olímpic marina area, and admire Frank Gehry's golden 'Fish' sculpture. The beachfront is a great place to people-watch and relax.
day_by_day.evening: Port Olímpic transforms into one of Barcelona's main nightlife hubs after dark. Enjoy sunset drinks at a chiringuito (beach bar) — budget €4–7 per drink. For nightlife, the clubs and bars around Port Olímpic and nearby Barceloneta get going from 23:00 onward. Many clubs have free entry before midnight or with a flyer — check local listings. Alternatively, the more local and budget-friendly nightlife scene is in El Raval (Carrer Joaquín Costa) or El Born.

meals.breakfast: Pick up supplies from a local supermarket (Mercadona or Lidl) the night before — fruit, yogurt, and pastries for a picnic breakfast in Parc Güell. Budget €3–5.
meals.lunch: Barceloneta beach area — avoid the overpriced beachfront restaurants. Walk one block inland for a menú del día at €12–14, or grab a bocadillo and eat on the beach.
meals.dinner: El Raval or El Born — budget tapas bars or a falafel/kebab for €8–12. Carrer del Parlament in Sant Antoni is a trendy but still affordable street for dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Book Parc Güell tickets online in advance — timed entry slots fill up quickly in August. Bring flip-flops or sandals for the beach. The metro Lesseps or Vallcarca stops are closest to Parc Güell. Stay hydrated — it will be very hot by midday.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Montjuïc hill — take the metro to Paral·lel and then the Funicular de Montjuïc (included with T-Casual metro card) up the hill. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró exterior and gardens (entry ~€14 if budget allows, or admire the architecture for free outside). Walk to the Castell de Montjuïc for panoramic views over the city and port — castle entry is €5 or free on first Sunday of the month. Explore the Olympic Stadium exterior (free) from the 1992 Barcelona Olympics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend Montjuïc and head to the Poble Sec neighborhood at the foot of the hill — one of Barcelona's most authentic and affordable barrios. Browse the Mercat de Sant Antoni (a beautifully restored iron market) for local produce and a cheap lunch. Spend the early afternoon doing any last-minute souvenir shopping — avoid La Rambla tourist shops; instead try El Born or Gràcia for affordable, locally made gifts. Pack your bags back at the hotel.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Barcelona — splurge slightly on a farewell dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Poble Sec or El Born (€18–25 per person). Poble Sec's Carrer de Blai is famous for its pintxos bars — an excellent budget option at €1.50–2.50 per pintxo. End the night with a walk along La Rambla (stay alert for pickpockets) and a final drink in the Gothic Quarter to soak in the atmosphere before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area café or supermarket — coffee and a pastry for €3–5.
meals.lunch: Mercat de Sant Antoni or a pintxos bar on Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec — budget €8–12.
meals.dinner: Carrer de Blai pintxos crawl for a fun, budget-friendly farewell meal — €15–20 including drinks, or a sit-down restaurant in Poble Sec for €18–25.

day_by_day.notes: Check your return flight details and plan transport back to the airport accordingly — allow at least 2.5 hours before departure. The L9 Sud metro to the airport runs regularly and costs ~€5.15 one way. Keep your T-Casual card if it has remaining trips. Tip: Barcelona's August nightlife is world-class — if you want a big night out, tonight is the night, but keep an eye on your belongings and budget for drinks (€6–10 each in clubs).

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus or taxi (~25 min) to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed evening stroll around the local neighbourhood to get your bearings.

meals.dinner: Casual dinner near the hotel: try La Taberna de Sant Just or a nearby neighbourhood tapas bar for patatas bravas, pan con tomate, and a glass of house wine. Budget ~€20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pick up a T-Casual metro card at the airport or a nearby tobacconist the next morning to save on transport costs throughout the trip. August evenings are warm (~24°C), so a light layer is all you need.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour (pre-booked skip-the-line tickets essential in August). Take the metro L5 from Cornellà Centre or a short bus ride into the city. Arrive early (~9:00) to beat the heat and crowds. Marvel at Gaudí's extraordinary unfinished basilica – the guided tour covers the nave, towers, and the fascinating museum in the crypt. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take a short taxi to Park Güell & Gràcia Neighbourhood Exploration. Explore the mosaic terraces, gingerbread gatehouses, and the Monumental Zone (timed entry ticket required). Afterwards, wander down into the charming Gràcia neighbourhood – browse its bohemian squares like Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, and pop into independent boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Head to El Born district for the Barceloneta Beach & El Born Nightlife Circuit. Start with a sunset stroll along Barceloneta Beach (golden hour ~20:30 in August), then transition into El Born for craft cocktails and bar-hopping. Try Bar del Pla or El Xampanyet for cava and pintxos before moving to livelier spots.

meals.breakfast: Café at the hotel or grab a croissant and café amb llet at a local bakery near the metro (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: Menú del día near Gràcia – a three-course set lunch with wine for ~€13–16 per person. Look for chalkboard signs on side streets off Carrer de Verdi.
meals.dinner: Tapas and pintxos in El Born at El Xampanyet (iconic, budget-friendly) or Bar del Pla. Budget ~€25–35 per person including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online well in advance – both sell out weeks ahead in August. Wear comfortable walking shoes and sunscreen; temperatures will peak around 29°C in the afternoon. Stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour. Start at 9:30 to explore the medieval labyrinth before the midday heat. Discover Roman ruins (Temple d'August), the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden courtyards. A guided tour (~2 hours) adds rich historical context, or self-guide with a downloaded audio tour app.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience on La Rambla. Arrive around 12:30–13:00 (locals' lunch hour – slightly less touristy). Sample fresh tapas, jamón ibérico, Manchego cheese, fresh fruit, and seafood at the market stalls. Afterwards, walk La Rambla toward the waterfront and visit the nearby Palau Güell (another Gaudí gem, often less crowded) for its rooftop chimneys and ornate interior.
day_by_day.evening: Return to El Born or head to Barceloneta for the nightlife circuit. Barcelona's nightlife starts late – dinner at 21:00, bars from 23:00, clubs from 01:00. Explore cocktail bars in El Born such as Paradiso (speakeasy-style, often ranked among Europe's best bars) or Rubi Bar for a more relaxed vibe.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at a café in the Gothic Quarter – try Cafè de l'Acadèmia area for a traditional Spanish breakfast of tostada with tomato and olive oil (~€5–8).
meals.lunch: Graze through La Boqueria – budget €15–20 for a satisfying spread of market bites, fresh juice, and a glass of cava.
meals.dinner: Sit-down dinner at a mid-range restaurant in El Born – try Bar Brutal (natural wines, creative tapas) or Llamber for modern Basque-Catalan cuisine. Budget ~€30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is best visited before 13:00 or after 16:00 to avoid peak tourist crowds. Keep an eye on your belongings on La Rambla – it is a known pickpocket hotspot. Paradiso bar has a queue system; arrive before 22:00 or expect a wait.

day_by_day.morning: Architecture deep-dive: Explore the Eixample district's Modernisme gems. Walk the 'Block of Discord' on Passeig de Gràcia – admire Casa Batlló (book a timed entry for the interior, ~€35), Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside. Continue to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) for a rooftop tour with its iconic warrior chimneys and panoramic city views. Allow the full morning (~3.5 hours).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax and recharge at Barceloneta Beach. Rent a sun lounger (~€6–8), swim in the Mediterranean, and enjoy the beach atmosphere. Alternatively, rent a bike along the seafront promenade and cycle toward the Forum district for a quieter beach experience. This is a great mid-trip rest afternoon given the August heat.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta & Port Olímpic nightlife. Watch the sunset from the beach (~20:30), then head to the Port Olímpic marina area for dinner with sea views, followed by the vibrant club scene. Pacha Barcelona or Opium are popular large-format clubs; for something more underground, check listings for events at Razzmatazz (a short taxi away in Poblenou).

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Federal Café in Sant Antoni (~€12–16) – avocado toast, eggs, and specialty coffee in a relaxed setting.
meals.lunch: Beachside chiringuito (beach bar) at Barceloneta – fresh grilled fish, calamari, and a cold beer or sangria. Budget ~€20–28 per person.
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at La Mar Salada or La Cova Fumada (cash only, arrive early – no reservations) near Barceloneta for authentic Barcelona seafood. Budget ~€30–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló and La Pedrera tickets should be pre-booked online. The magic hour rooftop experience at La Pedrera (evening ticket) is a popular alternative if you prefer a cooler visit. August rain is possible (47.5 mm monthly average) – carry a compact umbrella just in case.

day_by_day.morning: Montjuïc Hill exploration. Take the cable car or funicular up to Montjuïc for sweeping panoramic views of Barcelona and the port. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (world-class modern art, ~€14 entry) and the Castell de Montjuïc for history and views. A peaceful, scenic morning away from the city bustle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the city and explore the Sant Antoni neighbourhood – one of Barcelona's trendiest areas. Browse the renovated Mercat de Sant Antoni (Sunday market is famous, but the building is beautiful any day), visit independent concept stores, and enjoy a slow café stop. Pick up last-minute gifts or souvenirs at local design shops rather than tourist traps on La Rambla.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner and final night out. Splurge slightly on a memorable dinner at a well-regarded mid-range restaurant – Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample or Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca for excellent tapas and a festive atmosphere. End the night with a cocktail at a rooftop bar such as La Isabela at Hotel 1898 or Azimuth Rooftop for stunning city views as a final Barcelona memory.

meals.breakfast: Pastry and coffee at a neighbourhood café near the hotel – try an ensaïmada (Mallorcan pastry) or croissant de mantequilla (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Mercat de Sant Antoni area – a bocadillo (sandwich) or menú del día at a local bar (~€12–15).
meals.dinner: Farewell tapas feast at Cervecería Catalana – patatas bravas, croquetas, grilled vegetables, and jamón. Budget ~€30–40 per person including wine. Follow with a rooftop cocktail (~€12–15 per drink).

day_by_day.notes: Check your return flight details and plan transport back to the airport accordingly – allow at least 2.5 hours before departure. The Aerobus from Plaça de Catalunya takes ~35 minutes and costs ~€6.75. Store luggage at the hotel until departure if your flight is in the evening. August is peak season – enjoy every moment of this vibrant, sun-soaked city!

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 19:20
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — in transit from airport to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern. Allow approximately 30–40 minutes by private transfer from El Prat Airport. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.evening: Leisurely first-night dinner near the hotel to recover from travel. Explore the quiet upscale residential surroundings of Sant Just Desvern and enjoy a relaxed welcome to the Barcelona metropolitan area.

meals.dinner: El Racó de Can Fabes-style local gem: dine at Restaurant La Cantonada in Sant Just Desvern — a refined Catalan bistro offering seasonal tasting menus with local wines, perfect for a low-key luxury arrival dinner within minutes of the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private luxury transfer (e.g., via Blacklane or local concierge service) from Barcelona El Prat Airport to the hotel. Confirm hotel late check-in in advance. Keep the evening light — no heavy sightseeing after a long travel day. August evenings are warm (~24°C), so a short stroll around the hotel neighborhood is pleasant.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Begin the day with a skip-the-line premium guided tour of Gaudí's iconic unfinished basilica. Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the August crowds and the midday heat. Marvel at the Nativity and Passion facades, the soaring forest-like interior, and climb the towers for panoramic city views. A knowledgeable private guide will illuminate the symbolism and architectural genius behind this UNESCO World Heritage masterpiece.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell & Gràcia Neighborhood Exploration — After lunch, head to Gaudí's whimsical Park Güell. Explore the mosaic terraces, the iconic Dragon Stairway, and the Monumental Zone with reserved timed-entry tickets. Descend into the charming Gràcia neighborhood — browse its bohemian boutiques, admire the modernista architecture on Carrer de Provença, and relax at a shaded café in one of its lively plazas.
day_by_day.evening: Barceloneta Beach & El Born Nightlife Circuit — As the sun begins to set (~20:30), take a taxi or rideshare to Barceloneta Beach for a golden-hour stroll along the Mediterranean shore. Transition into the trendy El Born district for dinner and Barcelona's vibrant nightlife — cocktail bars, live music venues, and stylish clubs await.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby: Cafè de l'Acadèmia-style start — visit a specialty coffee shop in Sant Just Desvern or enjoy the hotel's breakfast service before heading into the city.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved Barcelona institution near the Eixample district, ideal between Sagrada Família and Park Güell. Order the patatas bravas, fresh seafood montaditos, and a glass of cava.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet in El Born — a legendary cava bar and tapas spot with decades of history. Follow with cocktails at Bar Paradiso (a speakeasy hidden behind a paella fridge) and late-night dancing at Razzmatazz or Sala Apolo.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets well in advance — August is peak season and tower access sells out weeks ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes; Park Güell involves uphill terrain. Carry a refillable water bottle — temperatures will reach ~29°C. The El Born nightlife scene typically starts after 22:00 and peaks after midnight.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Walking Tour — Immerse yourself in Barcelona's medieval heart with a premium private walking tour of the Gothic Quarter. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city streets, the magnificent Barcelona Cathedral, the ancient Jewish Quarter (El Call), Plaça Reial, and hidden courtyards that most tourists never find. A private guide adds rich historical context spanning 2,000 years of layered civilizations.
day_by_day.afternoon: La Boqueria Market Food Experience — A short walk from the Gothic Quarter along La Rambla leads to Barcelona's legendary Mercat de la Boqueria. Join a curated premium food experience: sample fresh jamón ibérico, artisan cheeses, Catalan charcuterie, exotic fruits, and freshly shucked oysters. Optionally pair with a private cooking class at a nearby culinary studio to learn to prepare classic Catalan dishes.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktails and fine dining in the Eixample district — Barcelona's modernista showpiece neighborhood comes alive at night. Enjoy pre-dinner drinks at the rooftop bar of the Hotel Majestic or Mandarin Oriental for sweeping city views, then dine at one of the Eixample's Michelin-starred restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Federal Café in Sant Antoni — a beloved Barcelona brunch institution known for its avocado toast, eggs Benedict, and specialty flat whites. A short taxi ride from the hotel.
meals.lunch: Light tapas and pintxos within La Boqueria or at Quimet & Quimet in Poble Sec — a legendary standing-room-only bodega famous for its creative montaditos and tinned seafood, paired with vermouth.
meals.dinner: Disfrutar Restaurant (2 Michelin stars) — one of Barcelona's most celebrated avant-garde dining experiences, run by alumni of elBulli. Book months in advance. The tasting menu (~€250 per person) is a theatrical journey through modern Catalan cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: La Boqueria is extremely crowded mid-morning in August — aim to arrive before 10:00 AM or after 14:00. Many market stalls are tourist-facing; a guided food experience ensures you access the authentic vendors. Disfrutar requires reservations made well in advance — confirm before the trip. Smart-casual to formal dress code for evening dining.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana & Modernisme Deep Dive — Begin with a guided tour of the breathtaking Palau de la Música Catalana, Lluís Domènech i Montaner's UNESCO-listed concert hall — a stained-glass and mosaic masterpiece. Afterward, embark on a self-guided or private Modernisme architecture walk along the Eixample's 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discordia): admire Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera in succession. Upgrade to the Casa Batlló premium night experience if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Montjuïc & MNAC — Take the Montjuïc cable car or a private car up to the hill overlooking the city. Visit the Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya (MNAC) for its world-class Romanesque art collection and the iconic building itself. Stroll through the Jardins de Laribal, visit the Fundació Joan Miró, and enjoy sweeping panoramic views of Barcelona's coastline and skyline from the castle ramparts.
day_by_day.evening: Poble Sec & Parallel Avenue Nightlife — Descend from Montjuïc into the hip Poble Sec neighborhood, Barcelona's emerging culinary and nightlife hotspot. Enjoy the vibrant tapas bar scene on Carrer de Blai (the 'pintxos street'), then head to the Parallel Avenue entertainment district for live shows, jazz bars, and late-night cocktail lounges.

meals.breakfast: Hofmann Pastisseria in the Gothic Quarter — an award-winning pastry school and café renowned for its croissants (voted among Spain's best), pastries, and excellent coffee. A perfect luxury morning treat.
meals.lunch: Tickets Bar (Albert Adrià) in Poble Sec — the playful tapas bar from the Adrià brothers offers a whimsical, avant-garde take on Spanish tapas. Reservations essential; book weeks ahead.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda in Eixample — a sophisticated wine bar and restaurant with an exceptional natural wine list and refined Catalan small plates. Follow with cocktails at Two Schmucks, one of the world's best cocktail bars, located in the Eixample.

day_by_day.notes: Casa Batlló's 'Magic Nights' evening experience (with augmented reality and live music) is a premium unmissable add-on — book separately. August heat peaks in the afternoon; Montjuïc's gardens offer shade and sea breezes. Two Schmucks is walk-in only — arrive before 21:00 to secure a spot or expect a queue.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely Luxury Morning & Spa — After four packed days, begin the final morning with a late, indulgent breakfast followed by a treatment at the hotel spa or a nearby luxury wellness center (e.g., Aire Ancient Baths Barcelona — a Roman-inspired thermal spa in the Gothic Quarter). This is a perfect way to recharge before a final afternoon of exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Poblenou & 22@ Innovation District Architecture Walk — Discover Barcelona's lesser-known architectural gem: the Poblenou neighborhood, once an industrial heartland now transformed into a cutting-edge design and tech district. Admire striking contemporary architecture including Jean Nouvel's Torre Agbar (Torre Glòries), the Rambla del Poblenou, and the innovative @22 urban regeneration projects. End with a final sunset walk along the Diagonal Mar waterfront and a swim at the quieter Nova Icària Beach.
day_by_day.evening: Grand Farewell Dinner & Skyline Nightcap — Celebrate the final evening with a world-class farewell dinner, followed by a nightcap at one of Barcelona's most spectacular rooftop bars with panoramic city and sea views.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel luxury breakfast or room service — indulge in a slow, lavish spread of fresh fruit, Catalan pastries, smoked salmon, and cava to mark the last morning.
meals.lunch: La Mar Salada near Barceloneta — an elegant seafood restaurant steps from the beach, celebrated for its arroz negro (black rice with cuttlefish), fresh grilled fish, and outstanding paella. Perfect for a final Mediterranean lunch.
meals.dinner: Lasarte Restaurant (3 Michelin stars, Chef Martín Berasategui) — the pinnacle of Barcelona fine dining. The multi-course tasting menu (~€300 per person with wine pairing) is an extraordinary farewell to the city. Follow with a nightcap at the rooftop bar of the W Barcelona Hotel (Hotel Vela) overlooking the illuminated harbor and Mediterranean Sea.

day_by_day.notes: Aire Ancient Baths should be booked in advance — the thermal circuit is 90 minutes and deeply relaxing. Lasarte is one of Spain's most decorated restaurants; reservations must be made months ahead and smart formal attire is required. If departing the following morning, arrange a private luxury transfer the night before. Pack light layers for the evening — August nights are warm but sea breezes can be refreshing.
